rendered:
The document does not show the wires being strained beyond 10%[1]. The authors state the opposite: tensile deformation was limited to that level. Their Methods say the surface coatings were strained up to 10%[2], and that "Tensile deformations beyond 10% were not[3] performed to avoid delamination of the coating from the wire surface[4]." So the limit was set to protect the coating from peeling off the wire, not to push the strain higher.

The top strain level was chosen for a different reason. The authors chose substrate strains of 5%[5] and 10%[6], "which would sufficiently exceed the saturation crack[7] density as reported for similar films deposited using ALD" (p3.L21). In other words, the strains were meant to be large enough to exceed the level needed to saturate cracking of the film. The Results describe the NiTi wire being subjected to axial tensile strains of 0−10%[8].
